guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
The old internal parent may demand immediate talent. The first awkward attempt becomes evidence that you are stupid, clumsy, or not “really” that kind of person. The adult has to protect the child from that verdict: “You’re allowed to be bad at this. We are finding out whether we enjoy it, not proving our worth.”
brief:
- the old internal parent may demand immediate talent (keep "may" and "immediate"; it's the internal one, now)
- the first awkward attempt becomes "evidence" that you're stupid, clumsy, or not "really" that kind of person (the critic's verdict, not a fact)
- the adult has to protect the child from that verdict as it lands, not only repair afterward ("has to" is firm)
- what the adult tells your little one: you're allowed to be bad at this; you're finding out whether you enjoy it, not proving your worth (an open question; "no" is a fine answer)
- context, not for the text: two first drafts of this paragraph failed the linter (more than 2 coach phrases per 100 words). Each put a "You might…" aside next to the quoted permission. Let the adult's quoted words carry the permission, and add no "You might…" or "You'll probably…" asides.
